text: dsh-pty-session 是面向 DSH 的终端会话插件，通过 owner-scoped PTY 服务注册 pty_open、pty_send、pty_tail 和 pty_close 工具，并提供供其他插件注入的 pty 服务。它可以启动命令、发送输入、增量读取新输出并关闭会话；会话按 agent 所有者隔离并可跨轮次保留。适合需要在 DSH 中持续交互式终端会话或构建终端消费者插件的场景。需在配置 bundle 中挂载 PTY 服务和后端。

dsh-pty-session adds interactive PTY sessions to DSH with tools to open, send input, tail output, and close. Sessions belong to the owning agent and persist across turns. Consumer plugins can use the same lifecycle through the provided pty service. Its bundle mounts the PTY service and backend.
想让 DSH 保留一个终端会话，后续还能继续发送命令。
需要在交互式 PTY 里启动命令并查看它刚产生的输出。
I want a DSH plugin to expose persistent, owner-scoped PTY sessions to other plugins.
dsh-pty-session 的功能「PTY 会话生命周期」：pty_open 在 PTY 上启动命令并返回会话 ID 与初始输出；pty_send 写入输入并返回输出增量；pty_close 结束会话。调用按 agent 所有者授权。
dsh-pty-session 的功能「增量读取终端输出」：调用 pty_tail 可按行数上限读取上次游标之后的新输出，并返回行数及是否截断；重复读取不会再次发送已消费的行。

dsh-pty-session README · dsh-pty-session：DSH plugin exposing the harness's **owner-scoped PTY seam** (`ctx.terminals`
— the same seam `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash-persistent` runs on) as four
protocol-agnostic tools: `pty_open` / `pty_send` / `pty_tail` / `pty_close`.

Layer 0 core: **byte-stream sessions with zero protocol knowledge**. Line
framing, REPL prompts, and protocol parsing (gdb/MI, ssh banners) belong to
consumer-layer plugins built on top of this surface.

dsh-pty-session README · API：| Tool | Args | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pty_open` | `command` (required), `cwd?`, `env?` | `sessionId`, `pid?`, `status`, `initialOutput` | Spawns on a PTY; `env` vars are exported (POSIX quoting) before the command on shell-type backends. Session survives turns. |
| `pty_send` | `id`, `data` (required), `submit?` (default `true`) | `delta`, `status` | Writes bytes; returns output read while the write settled. |
| `pty_tail` | `id` (required), `lines?` | `text`, `lines`, `truncated` | **Incremental cursor**: returns only new output since the last tail — repeated tails never resend. Backlog beyond `lines` returns the newest lines and sets `truncated: true`. |
| `pty_close` | `id` (required) | `closed` | Clean termination + reclaim. Idempotent per close. |

dsh-pty-session README · Lifetime & ownership：- Every call is authorized against the calling agent (`exec.agent`); another
  agent touching your session gets `FOREIGN_SESSION`.
- Sessions live with the **plugin instance**, not the turn: a fresh turn on
  the same agent sees all its open sessions.
- The owner-scoped registry closes all sessions when the owning agent
  disposes; the plugin additionally installs a dispose effect that closes
  every session it opened.

dsh-pty-session README · Semantics worth knowing：- **Lines, not bytes**: `pty_tail` inherits the seam's line-based scrollback
  contract (`totalLines`/`lineBegin`/`lineEnd`). Output without a trailing
  newline (a REPL prompt, a password prompt) becomes visible once its line
  completes. Byte-exact tail is the consumer layer's job if a consumer ever
  needs it.
- **`pty_send` submit**: defaults to `true` (backend Enter after the data) so
  interactive sessions behave; pass `submit: false` for byte-exact writes.
- **`pty_close`** delegates termination to the seam's awaited, idempotent
  cleanup (process-tree kill + quiescence) — the seam owns the mechanics.
- **`env`** is best-effort POSIX `export` lines and only meaningful on
  shell-type backends (the seam's spawn request has no env field); don't
  pass `env` against non-shell backends.

dsh-pty-session README · Configuration：```yaml
backendType: shell   # registered PTY backend type passed to terminals.spawn
tailLines: 200       # default pty_tail budget
```

dsh-pty-session README · Consumer-plugin facade (`ctx.pty`)：The facade exposes `open/send/tail/close/dispose` with EXACTLY the tool
semantics (same cursors, same seam reads — one core, two surfaces). The
owner is passed explicitly and must be the consumer's own `exec.agent`;
the seam enforces ownership (`FOREIGN_SESSION`). `close` is idempotent
(`closed:false` for an already-gone session). Loading this plugin becomes a
hard startup dependency of any consumer that injects `"pty"`.

dsh-pty-session README · Instance matrix：| Consumer | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| gdb (dsh-embedded-debug T5/T6) | **first consumer** — injects `ctx.pty` | MI framing lives in the consumer; API shape is being pressed out by gdb's needs. |
| ssh | **planned** — second consumer | Validates the abstraction once a second consumer exists. |
| serial (tio) / probe server / RTT | **explicitly excluded** | Non-PTY long-running processes: `job` + tail is already the correct pattern. |

dsh-pty-session README · Development：```sh
npm install        # vitest
npm test           # vitest run
```

Tests are the reference implementation: they drive the real tool surface
against a fake `terminals` registry whose backend runs **real interactive
child processes** (echo round-trips, no protocol parsing).

dsh-pty-session README · Harness deps (important)：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, and `@deepseek-ai/cordis`
must be **junctions/symlinks** into the installed harness's `node_modules`
(never copies): duplicated module instances make the DSH plugin loader fail
the entry with `failed to import`. On Windows:
